newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican separatists claim golf course blast.
newsitem.headline: Corsican separatists claim golf course blast.

text.p: Guerrillas of the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) claimed responsibility for a blast which destroyed a house at a golf course on the Mediterranean resort island on Thursday.
Five armed and masked men burst into the house of the Sperone golf course's keeper and blew it up with dynamite, a day after Corsican separatists vowed to step up their struggle against France.
The FLNC called a local television station to claim responsibility for the blast, which completely destroyed the house but injured no one.
The five men forced the keeper and two unidentified people who were with him to leave the house before placing the dynamite, police said.
The seaside golf course of Sperone has been hit by several blasts in the past, for which the FLNC also claimed responsibility.

The FLNC, which took its bombing campaign to the French mainland in September, said in a statement on Wednesday it planned "new forms" of attacks on the mainland and threatened local politicians and the families of paramilitary police on the Mediterranean island.
"Since (Prime Minister Alain) Juppe has opted for a military solution...we have decided to adapt our struggle on the ground with increased resources," the FLNC's hardline "historic wing" said.
The FLNC earlier took responsibility for a spectacular blast that wrecked Juppe's mayoral office in Bordeaux on October 5 as well as bombs in Marseille, Aix-en-Provence and Limoges last month.

The movement typically takes care to avoid civilian casualties but its threat added to the worries of police already on alert after a suspected Islamic fundamentalist bombing killed four people on a Paris underground train last week.
